findings.text: The `--description` value is passed through `eval "printf -v ... \"$2\""`. A test name containing `"`, `$(...)` or backticks, for example `@test "a\"; rm -rf ~; \""`, is executed as shell code. A name with an unmatched quote also causes an eval syntax error.

`[[ ${BATS_TEST_NAME-} == $* ]]` leaves `$*` unquoted, so the right side is treated as a glob pattern. A test name containing `*`, `?` or `[...]` can match a different test's name, and the wrong test then sets `BATS_TEST_COMMAND` and the tags. Names with spaces or special characters can also fail to match, because `$*` joins the arguments with spaces.

`bats_test_begin` is removed, but no caller is updated in this diff. Any preprocessor output or exec script that still calls `bats_test_begin` fails with command-not-found. That also drops the extended-syntax `begin` message and the call to `setup`.
